name: Vistra Corp.
monetization: Sells nuclear and gas power to hyperscalers under 20-year PPAs — >2,600MW to Meta across its PJM nuclear fleet, up to 1,200MW of Comanche Peak to Amazon — while buying gas fleets to serve data-center load.
description_md: Vistra is one of the largest competitive power generators in the US (~41GW across nuclear, gas, coal, solar, and storage), with nuclear plants including Comanche Peak (TX), Perry and Davis-Besse (OH), and Beaver Valley (PA) following its Energy Harbor acquisition. In the AI cycle it has become the second-largest hyperscaler nuclear counterparty after Constellation: 20-year PPAs with Meta totaling 2,609MW across its PJM nuclear fleet (January 2026) and a 20-year agreement with Amazon for up to 1,200MW from Comanche Peak. It is doubling down on dispatchable gas, agreeing in January 2026 to buy Cogentrix Energy's 5.5GW fleet for $4.7B after acquiring 2.6GW from Lotus Infrastructure in 2025.
ai_monetization_md: Two channels: (1) long-dated nuclear PPAs that convert merchant plants into contracted assets — Meta's 2,609MW package includes 1,268MW from Perry, 908MW from Davis-Besse, and 433MW of future uprates across Perry, Davis-Besse, and Beaver Valley, with full delivery of operating capacity by end-2027 and uprates through 2034; Amazon's Comanche Peak deal ramps from Q4 2027 to full capacity by 2032; and (2) merchant and contracted gas sales into ERCOT/PJM markets tightened by data-center load, which the Cogentrix and Lotus acquisitions (~8.1GW combined) are built to serve. PPA prices are undisclosed in both hyperscaler deals.
ai_strategy_md: Contract the nuclear fleet to hyperscalers at premium (undisclosed) prices, fund uprates against that committed demand, and grow the dispatchable gas fleet through M&A in the three markets with the heaviest data-center growth (PJM, ERCOT, ISO-NE). Unlike utilities, Vistra as an IPP captures scarcity pricing directly, making it one of the highest-beta listed plays on AI power demand.
risk_notes_md: Contract prices with Meta and Amazon are undisclosed — headline megawatts are known, economics are not. Uprate delivery (433MW for Meta, stretching to 2034) carries execution and NRC risk. The $4.7B Cogentrix deal (expected to close H2 2026, FERC/DOJ review pending) increases commodity-gas and acquisition-integration exposure and was premised on continued data-center load growth. Merchant upside works in reverse if AI demand or power prices soften.

events.title: Agrees to acquire Cogentrix Energy's 5.5GW gas fleet for $4.7B
events.why_it_matters: One of the first large AI-rationale power M&A deals: 10 modern gas plants across PJM, ISO-NE, and ERCOT bought explicitly to serve data-center-driven load growth; close expected H2 2026.

events.title: Meta signs 20-year PPAs for 2,609MW across Vistra's PJM nuclear fleet
events.why_it_matters: The largest multi-plant hyperscaler nuclear package to date — supports continued operation of Perry and Davis-Besse and funds 433MW of new uprate capacity against committed demand.

events.title: Amazon signs 20-year PPA for up to 1,200MW from Comanche Peak
events.why_it_matters: Extends hyperscaler nuclear contracting into ERCOT; disclosed alongside Q4/FY2025 results.
